37 An electrical device of fixed resistance 20  is connected in series with a variable resistor and a
battery of e.m.f. 16 V and negligible internal resistance.
16 V
20 
device
The power dissipated in the electrical device is 4.0 W.
What is the resistance of the variable resistor?
A
16 
B
36 
C
44 
D
64 

hints: Notice the $20 \, \Omega$ device and the variable resistor are in series, so they carry the same current but the $16 \text{ V}$ is shared between them.
Use the device power $4.0 \text{ W}$ with $P = I^2 R$ for the $20 \, \Omega$ resistor to find the series current.
Find the p.d. across the $20 \, \Omega$ device, subtract it from $16 \text{ V}$ to get the p.d. across the variable resistor, then use $R = V/I$.
walkthrough: The series loop has the $16 \text{ V}$ battery, the $20 \, \Omega$ device and the unknown variable resistor, so current $I$ is common and $16 \text{ V} = V_{device} + V_{variable}$.
For the device, $P = I^2 R$, so $4.0 = I^2 \times 20$. Hence $I = \sqrt{4.0/20} = \sqrt{0.20} \approx 0.447 \text{ A}$.
The p.d. across the device is $V_{device} = IR = 0.447 \times 20 \approx 8.94 \text{ V}$. Equivalently $V_{device} = \sqrt{PR} = \sqrt{4.0 \times 20} \approx 8.94 \text{ V}$.
The remaining p.d. must be across the variable resistor: $V_{variable} = 16 - 8.94 \approx 7.06 \text{ V}$.
So its resistance is $R = V_{variable}/I \approx 7.06/0.447 \approx 15.8 \, \Omega$, about $16 \, \Omega$. This is option A.

A.explanation: The current is about $0.45 \text{ A}$ and the p.d. across the variable resistor is about $7.1 \text{ V}$, giving $R \approx 16 \, \Omega$.

B.explanation: This adds the $20 \, \Omega$ device resistance to the $16 \, \Omega$ variable resistance instead of finding the variable resistance alone.

C.explanation: This incorrectly uses total power or total resistance from $16 \text{ V}$ and $4.0 \text{ W}$ without allowing for the $20 \, \Omega$ device sharing the e.m.f.

D.explanation: This incorrectly uses $P = V^2/R$ with the full $16 \text{ V}$ across the $20 \, \Omega$ device, which ignores the voltage drop across the variable resistor.
